newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Dec 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday on Canberra ABC radio that there would be no further Budget savings before the next Federal election. Howard believes the A$7.2 billion of cuts over two years included in the 1996/97 Budget should achieve a surpls in three years and the Government's fiscal targets should be met. Page 1.

After a marathon debate last night, the Senate gave its formal endorsement to the Federal Government's plan to sell a third of telecommunications giant Telstra. However, the Coalition did suffer a setback, with the Senate voting to retain an explicit Comonwealth power which will allow the Communications Minister to direct the board of the privatised company. Page 2

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday showed the residential housing market continued to steady in October, as the number of dwellings financed for purchase rose by 0.5 per cent compared to September. Page 4.

The three interest rate cuts this year should see property values for established houses, especially in Sydney and Melbourne, grow in the next 12 months. St George Bank economist Marcelle Basha said markets with strong demand and little oversupply shouldbenefit the most from the interest rate cuts. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In response to low inflation, the Reserve Bank yesterday announced it was reducing interest rates a further half a percentage point, sending home loan rates spiralling and allowing Prime Minister John Howard to take credit for "a magnificent Christmas present" for mainstream Australia. The cut brings rates down from 6.5 to six per cent. Page 1.

Australia's first CD-Rom World Encyclopedia, produced by Webster Publishing, was withdrawn from production yesterday after a display of the encyclopedia's entry on John F. Kennedy's funeral revealed Ted Kennedy giving his famous eulogy for Bobby Kennedy six years later. New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, who launched the product and had sent a copy to US President Bill Clinton, said it was a big mistake, one that Clinton would definitely pick up. Page 1.

The West Australian Labor Opposition effectively conceded defeat in the State's election yesterday, calling for a protest vote to deny the Coalition Government a "blank cheque" for a second term. Labor Leader Geoff Gallop's capitulation came as opinion polls indicated the Government may lose two safe Liberal seats to Independents. Page 1.

The Federal Government yesterday announced reforms to remove price controls from petrol and allow new players, such as food giant Woolworths, into the retail market, which should see motorists enjoying cheaper petrol. Prices will be deregulated next year once Federal Treasurer Peter Costello is satisfied the main four oil companies are letting competitors in the market to buy petrol at their terminals. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Official interest rates were cut to six per cent by the Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday, the lowest level in over 20 years. Major lenders have responded immediately, cutting home mortgage, credit card and business loan rates. The cut was the third in six months and came as a result of Australia's falling inflation rate, modest wage claims and high unemployment levels. Page 1.

An official study by the Australian Bureau of Statistics has found women are most vulnerable to violence at the places where they should be most safe: at the home and at work. The study found that just over seven out of every 100 Australian women over th age of 18 experienced some kind of violence in the 12 months before the study was conducted. Page 1.

A massive overrun in spending and a substantial write-down in the value of New South Wales' hospitals has seen the State's health budget blown out by A$450 million. The Health Department recorded a deficit of A$337 million instead of a projected surplus f A$116 million. Page 1.

Sydney councils have had enough of the dumping of supermarket trolleys from places such as the Harbour Bridge, by placing large fines on straying trolleys. Randwick Council has ordered a report into the problem, and Waverley Council is already charging aA$100 impounding fee for trolleys left in the street. Page 3.
THE AGE

A cut of 0.5 per cent in official interest rates by the Reserve Bank led to interest rate cuts on home mortgages, credit cards, and business loans yesterday. As the cut took rates down to six per cent, there are concerns the surging dollar could threatenthe economy, yet Prime Minister John Howard says the rate cut is an endorsement of his Government's low-inflation policies. Page A1.

In a 35-minute speech to Parliament yesterday, Prime Minister John Howard set the Government's goals for 1997 as boosting national savings, improving Australia's infrastructure and environment, and facilitating major investment projects to create jobs. Pae A1.

English-born Australian cricketer Andrew Symonds announced yesterday that he classed himself as Australian, and would therefore forgo a A$140,000 English country cricket contract and an English cap to play for Australia A against the West Indies today andmake himself available for Australian selection. Page A1.

An Australian Bureau of Statistics report entitled Women's Safety Australia has estimated that 500,000 women in Australia have experienced violence, threats or harassment in the past 12 months. The report surveyed 53,000 women over 18 and covered their eperiences of violence both as adults and children. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
